correctness.rationale: The ladder metric is exact and decomposes its distance-two adjacency graph into two P_n squares. The interval covering inequalities characterize every dominating subset of each square. A bijective bounded-deficit encoding proves the coefficient formula for all n, and its square counts independent pairs. Direct metric, subset, and composition computations independently corroborate the proof.

value.rationale: The all-n exact number of optimum configurations and the five-residue polynomial degree law quantify the multiplicity and rigidity of optimal exact-distance coverings of an elementary yet canonical narrow grid. Counts of minima are a natural companion invariant for new grid covering questions; an exact polynomial census is not implied by the literature's optimum-size bounds alone.
